chapter: C.L. Burke and Kid Ory years
title: Club Alabam, Curtis Mosby and the Plantation
summary: Burke's band ended at the Club Alabam under Curtis Mosby, and Blakeney and Redd sort out Mosby from Red Mack's brother Joe Morris of the Plantation.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I stayed with C.L. Burk three and a half years, ending at the Club Alabam on Central Avenue, L.A. The stay at the Alabam was very short due to the fact we were working for Curtis Mosby who was trying to stage a comeback in the nightclub form.
Mr. Curtis Mosby was very well known for his wheeling dealings in the area. I think he was the brother of Red Mack, who was--Mrs. Hightower taught Red Mack and Curtis Mosby was his brother.
I didn't know that. I knew he had two or three brothers, one of them Evans Mosby; you know him, don't you?

I've heard of him. Maybe we'll come back to that later, because their mother--the mother of Red Mack was a very well know real estate person during that time. He had nightclubs in the area, as I've been told, and also had his financial difficulties,which you are reiterating now.
I think you have the two nightclub owners mixed up.
Perhaps I do.
Curtis Mosby had the Alabam and Red Mack's brother owned the Plantation.
What was his name?
His name was Mosby--Morris was their last name, you know. I can't think of his name.
Perhaps it will come to you--to the two of us.
Red Mack, his name was McClure Morris, and his brother ran the Plantation out there on 107th and Central Avenue. Those are the two night-clubs I got mixed up.
The Plantation was further out on Central, way, way out.
107th And Central.
And the Club Alabam was in the heart of everything, on 42nd Place.
There is no relation between Curtis Mosby....
I know the gentleman's name--it was Joe Morris.
That's right. That's Red Mack's brother.
Right; and he owned the Plantation. I stand corrected, Mr.Blakeney.
That's right.
Was he involved in the Last Word nightclub?
He probably was because he was a tap dancer. He still is a tap dancer.
